gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's maker-store prices for the panel-to-station cables. On those stores, EcoFlow's Solar to XT60/XT60i cable is $24.99, BLUETTI's 30 A MC4 extension is $59 for 5 m or $79 for 10 m, and Jackery's 10 m extension is $59 but uses 14AWG wire. Meanwhile a 30 ft 10AWG MC4 pair (VEVOR) is $43.90 on vevor.com, cheaper than the $49.90 ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I compared against both cited pages and the top uncited result. yourpowersetup.com (cited) names the EcoFlow XT60/XT60i cable and Jackery DC7909-to-DC8020 guidance but gives no length, gauge, current rating or price. stormwatts.com/solar-panel-compatibility (cited) maps connectors to stations but has no cable gauge, rating or price. powerstationtips.com (uncited) has a gauge and voltage-drop table (10AWG for 25–50 ft) and two rough prices (~$19 for a generic MC4-XT60 cable, ~$25 for a Renogy 10 ft pair), but no maker cable prices and no Jackery wire gauge. Jackery's FAQ page in the results lists the 10 m cable's length, connectors and compatible stations, but not its gauge or price. None of these pages prices the maker cables today or notes that Jackery's 32.8 ft cable is 14AWG.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's main pick (a 10AWG MC4 extension) on price per foot: VEVOR's 30 ft 10AWG pair (30 A, 1500 V DC) is $43.90 on vevor.com, cheaper than BLUETTI's 5 m 30 A extension at $59. It also shows a weak spot in the brand-cable route for Jackery owners. Jackery's own 10 m DC8020 extension ($59) is 14AWG, the gauge powerstationtips' table puts at about 6% loss on a 50 ft run versus about 2% for 10AWG. It also corrects ChatGPT's EcoFlow card: EcoFlow's store lists the XT60i version at 2.5 m (8.2 ft), and 3.5 m is the older XT60 version.
